# RichTextEditor

RichTextEditor: a text field with a formatting toolbar, for where the formatting is part of the meaning.

**Import:** `import { RichTextEditor } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RichTextEditor/RichTextEditor.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RichTextEditor/RichTextEditor.stories.jsx` — Overview, Interactive, BlockStyleMenu, Empty, Filled, Focused, ReadOnly, DisabledState, Compact, FullToolbar, ToolbarButtonHovered, ToolbarButtonPressed

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/forms-and-inputs/RichTextEditor/RichTextEditor.mdx`

## Usage

Use a rich text editor where the formatting is part of the meaning: session notes with a list, feedback with emphasis, a description that needs a link. Where it is not, a text area is the smaller, sturdier control.

`toolbarPreset` is `compact` or `full`; passing `toolbarButtons` selects the buttons by name and implies the full toolbar. `value` and `onChange` are HTML strings. Giving it a `name` also renders a hidden input, so the HTML posts with a plain form.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name what the person writes: "Session notes". | "Editor" or "Text". |
| Use the placeholder for a hint about the content: "What did you cover?" | Repeat the label in the placeholder. |
| Offer only the buttons the content needs. | Every button by default. |
| Use sentence case and no end punctuation on the label. | Title case, or a period after the label. |

## Best practices

### Use the compact toolbar for short notes. {#use-the-compact-toolbar-for-short-notes}

Fewer tools keep a short field light.

Do: The compact toolbar on a short note.
Don't: The full toolbar on a short note.

### Use the full toolbar for long content. {#use-the-full-toolbar-for-long-content}

Long-form writing needs the full set of tools.

Do: The full toolbar for a long summary.
Don't: Long-form writing limited to the compact toolbar.

### Use read-only for content people read. {#use-read-only-for-content-people-read}

Set `readOnly` on content people need to read, and keep `disabled` for an editor that is unavailable. Both draw the same here, so the choice is about what the content is for.

### Use the placeholder for a hint. {#use-the-placeholder-for-a-hint}

Do: The placeholder hints at what to write.
Don't: The placeholder repeats the label.

### `value` is written to the DOM as HTML. {#value-is-written-to-the-dom-as-html}

```jsx
// Incorrect: the value is assigned to the editable region's innerHTML, so
// anything a user can influence is executed as markup.
<RichTextEditor value={note.bodyFromApi} onChange={setBody} />

// Correct: sanitize on the way in, and again on the way out before storing.
<RichTextEditor value={sanitize(note.bodyFromApi)} onChange={(html) => setBody(sanitize(html))} />
```

The same applies to what you receive: `onChange` hands you whatever the browser produced, which is markup from a paste as much as from the toolbar.

### It is built on a deprecated browser API. {#it-is-built-on-a-deprecated-browser-api}

Formatting runs through `document.execCommand`, which every engine now documents as deprecated. It works today and its exact output differs between browsers: one may wrap a line in `<div>`, another in `<p>`. Do not depend on the shape of the HTML; store it and render it, or convert it once on save.

### Link and image ask with a browser prompt. {#link-and-image-ask-with-a-browser-prompt}

Pressing those buttons opens the platform `prompt()` dialog for a URL. It is unstyled, it is not translatable, and some environments suppress it. Where that matters, leave those two buttons out of `toolbarButtons`.

### Label the editor. {#label-the-editor}

Do: A label names the editor on screen and for assistive technology.
Don't: No label, only a placeholder, which disappears as soon as someone types.

## Accessibility

- **The editable region announces itself as a multi-line textbox.** `role="textbox"` with `aria-multiline`, and `aria-readonly` tracking the flag that turns editing off.
- **`label` names it, and is effectively required.** The prop renders a `span` above the editor and the region points at it with `aria-labelledby`. A `label` element cannot be used, because `contentEditable` is not a form control for `htmlFor` to bind to. Without a `label` the region is a named role with no name, which a screen-reader user hears as nothing.
- **The toolbar buttons are named.** Each carries an `aria-label` from its definition, and the bold, italic and underline set is a `role="group"` labeled "Bold, italic, and underline". Their pressed state is tracked internally and is not exposed as `aria-pressed`.
- **The placeholder is CSS.** It is drawn from a `data-placeholder` attribute, so it is not part of the accessible name and may not be announced at all.
- **Keep the formatting optional.** Anything that only exists as bold text or a color in the body is invisible to someone hearing the page. Structure it with lists and headings instead.

## Related

- For plain multi-line text, use Text area: smaller, labeled, and with none of the above.
- For one line, use Text field.
- For displaying formatted content the user cannot edit, render the HTML yourself after sanitizing it.
